# `aitbc network gossip`

Show gossip websocket health: which validators have authenticated, and traffic. Reports the *inbound* side of gossip - the public `/rpc/gossip/ws` endpoint this node serves to its peers - by joining the validator set from /rpc/network-info against the auth counters on /metrics. A healthy node shows one authenticated peer per *other* validator: a node never dials its own websocket, so exactly one validator row is expected to read `no`. Two or more mean a peer is not reaching this node. This does not cover the node process's *outbound* mesh links. Those live in aitbc-blockchain-node, which serves no HTTP endpoint; check them with scripts/monitoring/fleet-config-check.sh, which reads GOSSIP_MESH_PEER_URLS from the running process.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc network gossip [OPTIONS]
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--rpc-url` | text | `http://localhost:8202` | no | Blockchain RPC URL <!-- check-ports: ignore --> |
| `--topics` | flag | `false` | no | Also break published message counts down by topic |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc network gossip
RPC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8202/rpc
aitbc network gossip --rpc-url "$RPC_URL"
```
